dataset.name: Fake and Real News Dataset

source_used.source: local data/ copies (previously downloaded from mirror below)

dataset.labels_note: Labels are as provided in the source files, not independently verified.

steps: missing title/text/subject/date filled with empty string
rows with empty combined text removed
exact duplicate title+text pairs removed (before splitting, so no leakage)
lowercased, URLs removed, punctuation removed, extra spaces collapsed
stop-word removal by TF-IDF vectorizer (English stop words)

split_FR04.method: stratified 80/20, random_state=42, split BEFORE fitting TF-IDF

error_analysis_FR07.note: Errors are mostly on short / opinion-heavy pieces and on subjects where fake and genuine writing styles overlap (e.g. politics). A single short headline alone is much less reliable than a full article.

robustness_FR08.method: same 200 test articles, prediction compared before/after a trivial change
robustness_FR08.interpretation: Capitalisation should not matter (text is lowercased). Extra spaces / punctuation should change almost nothing, because TF-IDF tokenises on word boundaries.

robustness_and_subject_note: Subjects and years come from the source files. Fake and genuine files use different subject vocabularies (e.g. 'politics' vs 'politicsNews'), so subject comparisons describe the data as-is and are not a clean causal test.

model_export_FR10.verified_agreement_with_sklearn: 200/200 test articles (100%) on a 200-item sample, checked 2026-11-08

limits: Trained on 2015-2018 US political news; it will be much less reliable on other topics, languages, or recent news.
It learns writing style / textual patterns, not facts — a well-written fake can pass and a poorly written genuine article can fail.
Short headlines alone are far less reliable than a full article.
Labels in the source dataset were not independently verified by us.
performance_by_year_best_model_note: Only 2078 of 7766 test articles have a parseable year; date column has mixed formats and a few polluted values, so year results cover that subset only.
